subject: Career
title: The T-Shaped Professional
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The T-Shaped Professional.

hook.text: Deep expertise in one area plus broad knowledge across many — that's the T-shaped professional.

buildup.text: The concept originated at McKinsey: hire people who are deep specialists with wide-ranging curiosity.

discovery.text: T-shaped professionals adapt to transitions because their broad base connects to many industries.

twist.text: An I-shaped person (deep but narrow) struggles to pivot. A dash-shaped person (broad but shallow) lacks credibility.

climax.text: Build your T: go deep in one domain while learning the basics of adjacent fields.

punchline.text: Go deep enough to be an expert. Go wide enough to adapt.

quiz.question: What defines a T-shaped professional?
options: Deep expertise in one area plus broad knowledge across many

details.summary: A T-shaped professional has deep expertise in one area combined with broad knowledge across many disciplines. This profile makes career transitions easier because the horizontal bar provides multiple entry points into new fields.
details.whyItMatters: Specialists without breadth struggle to pivot because they have only one deep skill. T-shaped professionals can leverage their broad base to enter adjacent fields quickly.
takeaways: The vertical bar represents deep mastery in one domain
The horizontal bar represents broad cross-functional literacy
T-shaped profiles are increasingly valued in collaborative work

faq.question: How do you build the horizontal bar of the T during a busy career?
faq.answer: Volunteer for cross-functional projects, attend talks outside your department, and dedicate a few hours weekly to learning adjacent disciplines. The goal is functional literacy, not mastery, so even shallow exposure across many fields adds significant value.

faq.question: Is it better to be T-shaped or to have deep expertise in multiple areas?
faq.answer: Multiple deep areas create a pi-shaped or comb-shaped profile, which is even more transition-friendly. However, building deep expertise takes years, so T-shaped is the most practical starting point for most professionals.
